newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: South African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares returned to just below their previous closing levels at the end of trade on Monday after a day of choppy dealings.
Gold shares shrugged off fresh lows in the bullion price which in the morning fixed at $370.50 per ounce -- its lowest level since April 25, 1994.
After beginning the day softer, gold stocks ended steady propped up by a weaker rand, which slid over four cents against the dollar on Monday, dealers said.
"The gold price is abysmal, but the rand stopped shares from sinking," a dealer said.
Traders said interest in gold shares, on both the selling and the buying side, had been thin.
"When it comes to gold shares, people are keeping their hands in their pockets," a trader said.
The gold index finished only 0.7 points weaker at 1,523.4. Vaal Reefs was one rand down at 320 rand, Loraine up 10 cents at 14 rand and Kloof 45 cents softer at 37.35 rand.
Initially boosted by arbitrage trading between the futures and spot market, industrial shares ended a touch weaker but off their lowest levels reached when the rand lost ground.
"In the morning industrials were driven by futures demand. But this was overdone and a foreign seller of futures came into the market, and demand for index-linked stocks dried up," a dealer said.
Traders said the softer rand further punctured industrials' early gains.
But stocks again retraced off their weaker levels as interest dried up later in the afternoon, they said.
The industrial index finished 4.7 points down at 7,992.8, after at one stage being up over 35 points.
Amongst key stocks, SAB added 75 cents to 117 rand, Remgro lifted 70 cents to 42 rand after reporting better-than-expected first half results but Amic shed 125 cents to 168.50 rand.
Traders said October trade data released on Monday which showed a shock 3.9 billion rand surplus -- three billion rand more than forecast -- had little effect on the market.
"The figures are so volatile from month-to-month that people don't really react to them," a trader said.
Gold stocks were expected to soften on Tuesday if bullion probed below the $370 level, while industrials were seen losing ground on an ailing rand.
December industrial equity futures contracts fell in afternoon trade as a foreign seller appeared in the market, dealers said. Golds stayed weak on the bullion price.
The near-month industrial contract was last at 7,721/28 from 7,759 on Friday, the gold contract was at 1,057/75 from 1,073 previously and the all-share was unchanged at 6,176.
